**Most euro area payment providers now respond to verification of payee checks**

*The instant payments regulation's verification of payee mandate is being met across most of the euro area, though gaps remain in smaller markets.*

The majority of euro area payment service providers are now answering verification of payee requests, according to data reported by The Paypers. The figures indicate that the mechanism, which matches a payee's name to their IBAN before a transfer is executed, has reached broad operational coverage ahead of the regulation's full enforcement timeline.

Coverage varies by market. Larger euro area economies appear to have achieved near-complete participation, while some smaller or more recently integrated markets still show gaps. The data provides the first clear picture of how far the industry has come since the instant payments regulation mandated the service, and where remediation work remains.

The practical question is now shifting from whether providers can answer checks to how accurately they do so. Persistent matching errors in IBAN-name verification have been a recurring concern, and the quality of responses will matter as much as their availability once enforcement intensifies.

*Sources: [Most euro area payment providers now answer VoP checks, data shows](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/most-euro-area-payment-providers-now-answer-vop-checks-data-shows) — The Paypers*

**ECB approves Revolut's partial transfer of Lithuanian banking operations to France**

*The approval formalises a dual-hub model that will see Western European customers migrate from Vilnius to Paris, reshaping Revolut's regulatory footprint across the EU.*

The European Central Bank has approved the cross-border reorganisation of Revolut Bank UAB, enabling the fintech to transfer part of its Lithuanian entity's assets and liabilities to Revolut Bank SA, the French banking subsidiary licensed in August. The Bank of Lithuania's Legal and Licensing Department submitted the formal notice to Lithuania's Centre of Registers on November 6, following the ECB's approval on October 22.

French customers will be the first to migrate to Revolut Bank SA, with Germany, Ireland, Italy, Portugal and Spain to follow in subsequent phases. Revolut Bank UAB will continue serving customers across the rest of the European Economic Area. Revolut has said that neither Lithuanian employees nor Lithuanian customers will be affected, and that its plans to expand and launch new services in Lithuania remain unchanged.

The restructuring marks a significant evolution in how Europe's largest neobank organises itself within the single market. Rather than passporting services from a single licence — the approach most fintechs have used since PSD2 — Revolut is building a two-centre model with separate supervised entities in Vilnius and Paris. With more than 75 million customers globally, the company's decision to anchor its Western European operations under direct French and ECB supervision reflects both the scale it has reached and the regulatory complexity that comes with it.

*Sources: [ECB clears partial move of Revolut's Lithuanian operations to France](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/ecb-clears-partial-move-of-revoluts-lithuanian-operations-to-france) — The Paypers*

stories.original:
**Affirm acquires Nexi's Ratepay to enter Germany's pay-by-invoice market**

*The deal gives the US buy now, pay later provider an established position in German-speaking Europe's distinctive invoice payments segment, while Nexi sheds another non-core asset.*

Nexi has agreed to sell Ratepay, a Berlin-based pay-by-invoice specialist serving merchants in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, to Affirm. The two companies have also signed a memorandum of understanding to expand their existing commercial partnership across the DACH region. Financial terms were not disclosed. Completion is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

Bernardo Mingrone, chief executive of Nexi, said the divestment was "in line with our strategy focused on core activities and optimized portfolio". Nexi had already classified Ratepay as non-core and restructured the business, reducing its workforce by roughly 20%. The sale continues the pattern set at Nexi's capital markets day: disciplined disposal of peripheral operations in favour of payment processing and acquiring.

For Affirm, Ratepay offers a ready-made route into a market where paying after receiving goods remains a dominant checkout method. Pat Suh, Affirm's senior vice president and managing director of global markets, said the company's focus is on expanding merchant and consumer trust. Under Affirm's ownership, Ratepay plans to add instalment products alongside its existing invoice capability. Affirm said the acquisition is not expected to materially affect its financial results or its outlook for the 2027 financial year.

*Sources: [Nexi agrees Ratepay sale to Affirm, signs MoU on DACH partnership](https://thepaypers.com/mergers-aquisitions-and-investments/news/nexi-agrees-ratepay-sale-to-affirm-signs-mou-on-dach-partnership) — The Paypers*
